failures.triage_note: Low severity, not a security hole: the security invariant (no asset served, no 500) fully holds; only the documented HTTP status code differs. Likely the runbook contract text needs updating to match current (arguably more correct) behavior rather than the code needing a fix -- 400 for a malformed/incomplete request is defensible REST semantics.
failures.expected: GET /wp-json/mvs/v1/serve?mvs_id={private_id} with no mvs_uid/mvs_exp/mvs_sig params returns HTTP 403 (per runbook C.member.signed-url: 'logged-out viewer with no token returns 403, not the asset, not a 500').
failures.actual: Returns HTTP 400 rest_invalid_param / rest_missing_callback_param ('Missing parameter(s): mvs_uid, mvs_exp, mvs_sig') because those three params are registered as REQUIRED route args, so WP's REST arg validation rejects the request before the permission/signature check ever runs. No asset is served and no 500 occurs, but the status code is 400, not 403.

failures.triage_note: Low severity, no customer-facing impact. Re-confirmed live this run (independent of the prior 12:15 report): the real, displayed comment count comes from mvs_media_stats.comments, which DOES update correctly on comment create/delete and is what MediaController's REST response and the grid UI actually read. mvs_media_index.comment_count is a separate denormalized column defined in the schema but has no writer anywhere in includes/ after its default 0 (grepped includes/Social/CommentService.php and callers -- no UPDATE touches this column). Contrast with the sibling reaction_count column, which ReactionService keeps in sync. Worth a one-line fix or dropping the column; not a release blocker.
failures.expected: mvs_media_index.comment_count either stays in sync with real comment activity (matching the reaction_count pattern) or is removed if genuinely unused.
failures.actual: Posted a real comment on media_id=123 via POST /mvs/v1/media/123/comments (id=4, cleaned up after) -- mvs_media_stats.comments went 0 to 1 correctly, but mvs_media_index.comment_count for the same media_id stayed at 0 throughout.
